item.title: Iran won't escalate tensions but will defend itself, says Pezeshkian amid Trump's warning
item.description: Iran states it will defend its security while the US president claims a last chance for a deal. Conflicting reports emerge regarding ongoing negotiations between Iran and the United States. Shipping activity through the Strait of Hormuz remains subdued amid these diplomatic claims. Iran's IRGC reportedly launched a drone attack on a US military base in Kuwait. Tehran also prepared retaliatory strikes on Ukraine after a vessel incident.

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg's wife invested $125 million in a school for the disadvantaged; now she is closing it to focus on AI
item.description: The Primary School, offering tuition-free education to low-income families, has officially closed, impacting around 540 children who depended on its support. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, the school's benefactor, is redirecting its resources towards biotechnology and artificial intelligence. As part of its commitment, it has announced substantial funding aimed at assisting affected students and local organizations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Europe's shrinking rivers have hit shipping, power and tourism
item.description: Record low water levels in Europe's major rivers are disrupting electricity production, cargo transport and business operations as heatwaves and drought continue across the continent. Nuclear and hydropower plants have cut output, shipping on the Danube and Rhine has slowed, and companies are reporting lower earnings, highlighting the growing economic impact of prolonged extreme weather
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Countries with most black mambas: From South Africa to Kenya, where the deadly snake is found
item.description: The black mamba, often cited as the most dangerous snake on the African continent, occupies a wide array of habitats. This snake thrives in arid savannas and rocky terrains throughout sub-Saharan Africa. Countries such as South Africa and Zimbabwe frequently report incidents of black mamba bites. Remarkably, sightings have increased in Kenya and Zambia at higher altitudes, with Tanzania and Botswana also within its expansive territory.

item.title: Russia downs 320 drones: Six killed, warehouses damaged in Moscow, St Petersburg
item.description: Russia’s defence ministry said it brought down or destroyed 320 Ukrainian drones across 19 regions overnight, as governors reported six people killed, nine injured and warehouses damaged near Moscow and St Petersburg.

item.description: Federal officers seized more than $20 million in cocaine hidden beneath the floorboards of a commercial truck carrying 269 bundles of rebar at California’s Calexico border crossing, arresting the driver after finding 366 packages of narcotics.

item.title: 'I will fight tooth and nail': Brewery owner who offered free beer if Trump died, loses licence
item.description: Kirk Bangstad, owner of Wisconsin's Minocqua Brewing Company, has vowed to "fight tooth and nail" after the state revoked his brewery's operating permits. The action follows allegations that the company illegally transported beer from Illinois without the required permits or paying taxes. Bangstad, whose brewery previously made headlines for promising free beer if Donald Trump died, called the revocation an "absurd act of heavy-handedness" and plans to appeal.

item.title: Video of dolphin carrying its dead newborn through the Indian Ocean reveals a deep and old 'mourning ritual'
item.description: Fraggle, a grieving mother dolphin, carried her deceased calf for six days, a poignant testament to her profound maternal love. Captured by drone footage in the Indian Ocean, this heart-wrenching scene revealed the support of her pod, which gathered around her in solidarity during her mourning. This behavior, seen in over twenty cetacean species, underscores their intricate social connections and possible awareness of mortality.

item.title: Florida's first flesh-eating bacteria death of 2026
item.description: Florida health officials confirmed the state's first 2026 Vibrio vulnificus fatality. This flesh-eating bacteria thrives in warm coastal waters during summer months. Individuals with weakened immune systems face significantly higher risks. Public awareness is crucial as cases double during the peak season.

item.title: US moves closer to deep-sea mining near American Samoa with 31.5 million acre lease plan
item.description: The United States has moved a step closer to deep-sea mining after the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) proposed auctioning two massive seabed lease areas near American Samoa for mineral exploration. The proposal marks a significant milestone in the country's efforts to secure critical mineral supplies for clean energy, electronics and national security.

item.title: Colombia intercepted a boat near the Malpelo sanctuary carrying 1,764 pounds of marine animals
item.description: Colombian authorities have intercepted a fishing vessel carrying approximately 1,764 pounds of suspected illegally caught marine animals believed to have been taken from the protected Malpelo Fauna and Flora Sanctuary, bringing renewed attention to illegal fishing in one of the country's most ecologically important marine reserves.
